title: The Persistent Widow (vertical, components)

opening.text: Some prayers we quietly stop praying, because nothing changes.
Jesus tells of a judge who could be bought.
And a widow with nothing to pay, who keeps coming back.
In this devotional, we look at who this judge really was.

reflection.text: Jesus wants his disciples to keep praying, and for his example he picks a judge who says himself that he fears neither God nor people.
Why him, of all people?
To Jesus' first hearers, this judge was a familiar kind of man.
One person sitting alone was not how a Jewish court worked, unless both sides had chosen him themselves.
And this man does not speak or act like someone bound by the Law of Moses.
He was more likely an official appointed by Herod or by Rome.
People joked about paid judges, with a play on words that turned them into judges of robbery.
Village judges, they said, would change a verdict for a dish of meat.
Justice went to whoever could pay.
The widow had nothing to pay with.
All she had was her voice, and she used it until hearing her again cost the judge more than ruling for her.
Now we can see why Jesus chose him.
Not to say that God is like him, but to show how far apart they are.
If even this judge gives in to someone he does not care about, how much more will God answer his own children.
He is the righteous Judge, and he is a loving Father.
Look at how Jesus describes God's people in verse seven.

callout.text: Will not God bring about justice for His elect who cry out to Him day and night? Will He delay in helping them?

reflection.text: Not by how strong they are, or by how many answers they have had.

reflection.text: That is why the story ends the way it does.

reflection.text: What is left open is whether we will still be asking when he comes.

reflection.text: The widow kept coming to a corrupt judge, with nothing in her hands.
We come to a Father who cannot be bought and does not need to be.
The judge gave in to be rid of her.
God answers because he loves his children.
And the One who told this story is the One who will come, hoping to find us still asking.

takeaway: With that judge, the verdict was in doubt. With God, the only question is whether we stay persistent in prayer.

verse.text: “Be joyful in hope, patient in affliction, persistent in prayer.”

question: What is the one request you have quietly stopped bringing to God because the answer seemed slow?
prayer: Bring that request back to God today and tell him honestly how long the wait has felt. Ask him for the faith to go on asking.
